hero.title: Kaikou Nuo
hero.subtitle: A village ritual in which masked characters sing and speak

paras: Kaikou Nuo is a form of masked ritual theater practiced in Wanzai. Also known locally as Tiaoxiao, it was performed to ward off misfortune and pray for peace. The tradition is traced to the transition from the Yuan to the Ming dynasty.

Kaikou means “open mouth,” referring to the performers’ singing and speech. The repertoire brings together singing, spoken lines, stylized movement and stage combat, with percussion accompanying the performers.
In June 2008, Wanzai’s Kaikou Nuo was added to China’s national intangible cultural heritage list under Nuo theater.
